title: Donovan Mitchell agrees to 4-year, $273 million extension with Cavaliers: Source
content:
The Cleveland Cavaliers and star guard Donovan Mitchell agreed on a four-year, $273 million contract extension Tuesday that could keep him on the shores of Lake Erie through the 2031 season, two league sources granted anonymity because the team has not announced the extension confirmed to The Athletic.

Mitchell, 29, a nine-time All-Star who is already statistically one of the greatest Cavaliers ever, became eligible to receive a contract extension Tuesday. The deal includes a player option for the 2030-31 season. ESPN first reported the agreement.

The extension for Mitchell won’t kick in until the 2027-28 season and doesn’t impact the one guaranteed season left on his current contract for $50.1 million. Mitchell’s player’s option is for the 2030-31 season, at $75 million, when he would be 34-years old.

Mitchell, whom the Cavs traded for in the summer of 2022, could have waited a year and signed a five-year, $353 million extension with the Cavs next summer as a 10-year vet. Instead, Mitchell opted for financial security and protection against injury, while at the same time, confirming what he’s been telling The Athletic all along — he really likes it in Cleveland.

“This is an organization that’s willing to do (anything) for its players,” Mitchell told The Athletic in April.

Mitchell has averaged 26.7 points, 5.3 assists, 4.6 rebounds, and 1.5 steals per game while shooting 46.9 percent from the field across his 264 regular-season games for the Cavaliers since his trade from the Utah Jazz in 2022. Cleveland has reached the postseason in each of his four seasons there, and last season reached the conference finals for the first time since 1993 without LeBron James on the roster.

Last season was also Mitchell’s first time getting to the conference finals, even though his teams have reached the postseason in each of his nine years in the NBA.

Speaking of James, the agreement between the Cavs and Mitchell is a great start to a potentially monumental week for Cleveland. The Cavs are also hoping James, 41, picks them in free agency, which would create a workplace marriage of the forever and current faces of the franchise. James was Mitchell’s favorite player as a teenager growing up outside of New York City.

Outside of James’ looming decision, Cleveland will soon ink another future hall of famer, James Harden, to a lucrative, multiyear contract. The Athletic previously reported that Harden’s new deal with the Cavs, whom he has played for since Cleveland traded for him at the February deadline, has been agreed to in principle — but the two sides are waiting to finalize it so the organization can have maximum flexibility to make another move. Like signing LeBron.
